A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GenZ-LTL. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison; v6 additionally includes a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v4 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments in LetterWorld and ZoneEnv, including benchmark comparisons, ablations and supplementary Ant-agent evaluations.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results in the main text and Appendix C. Retained results still qualify as original empirical evidence.

M1.justification: Subgoal construction, observation reduction, reachability learning and timeout switching remain unchanged, as do Algorithms 1–2 and the optimized surrogate in Eq. (3). The formal KL-constraint refinement in Eq. (2) does not establish a changed training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same environments, LTL specifications, partial observability, overlapping regions, additional propositions and Ant dynamics. The new main-text reference to Ant experiments summarizes evaluations already present in v4 Appendix C.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments, including the four finite-horizon baselines and the DeepLTL comparison for Ant dynamics. Adding the RAD-embeddings code-source footnote does not add a baseline.

E3.justification: Training budgets, architectures, environment configurations, evaluation metrics, trajectory counts and testing procedures are retained. Deterministic evaluation, extended horizons and the supplementary experimental settings were already documented in v4.

E4.justification: The observation-reduction and safety ablation, complexity tests, timeout evaluation, partial-observability and overlap analyses, stochastic-policy comparison and Ant analysis are retained. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: New checklist item 7 describes the reported statistics as means and variances across runs. Existing five-seed averages, ± entries and uncertainty bands are unchanged; the added description does not establish additional runs or new statistical tests.

E6.justification: All result-table entries match: v4 Tables 1, 2, 7 and 8 correspond to v6 Tables 2, 3, 6 and 7. Empirical plots, trajectory illustrations and reported findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Eq. (2) adds an explicit expectation over uniformly sampled subgoals and on-policy states to the KL-divergence constraint, where v4 states the bound without that expectation. This is a limited formal revision; the remaining assumptions and derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The claims of arbitrary-LTL zero-shot generalization through safe single-subgoal learning, observation reduction and timeout switching remain. The contribution bullets and conclusion are unchanged; the rewritten introduction emphasizes existing claims.

C2.justification: Both retain the greedy-search failure caveat, observation-symmetry requirements, difficulties with unseen sensing modalities, and interpretations of safety and stochastic-policy results. The checklist largely restates existing limitations and broader-impact discussion.

D1.justification: v6 adds a GenZ-LTL repository address in the abstract and identifies the official RAD-embeddings implementation in Appendix B. v4 already mentions supplementary code; network architectures, hyperparameters, hardware and runtime remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 61 references and related-work discussion are retained. The rewritten introduction highlights relationships to subgoal decomposition, automaton embeddings and HJ reachability already established in v4, without changing novelty claims.

P1.justification: v6 rewrites the introduction's method-summary paragraph, adds a pointer to existing Ant results, updates affiliations and acknowledgements, and appends the NeurIPS checklist. Most prose and the main section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v6 adds the observation-reduction diagram in Figure 2 and merges v4's specification Tables 3–4 into main-text Table 1, abbreviating color names. Figure 1 relabels Evaluation as Testing; retained displays are renumbered and reflowed.

improvement.justification: The new observation-reduction diagram and consolidated specification table make the method and evaluations easier to follow. Repository pointers improve code-access documentation, and Eq. (2) makes the KL averaging explicit. These are useful, limited improvements; the experimental evidence and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
